answer: Each identity posts a bond whose signing key sits in a hardware root, so a second account needs a second physical chip. Audit panels clear a diversity check first; if three jurors trace to one operator, the bond is voided. Trust attaches to a finished task, not an address, so a terrace of clones earns zero until each ships work. Under inspection the clones show the same pigment as the machine that made them, and the panel logs it. Price it: one chip, one bond, one cipher solved per account.
